A map of open questions in physics

Choose a window into gravity, particles or cosmic history. Each shows a different piece of work needed before the explanation can go further.

The sky is an illustration. These are open research questions, not discoveries already made. They can still help someone choose a calculation or observation worth trying.

Choose a research question. Read what would still be needed to answer it.

Words used here
cosmology
The study of the universe’s large-scale structure and history.
model
A simplified description used to explore a question. A result in the model needs further evidence before it describes the real world.
Read the fuller explanation

The target map includes gravity and torsion, flavour and neutrino structure, joined cosmological likelihoods and continuum control. Each carries a different missing obligation. A shared word or symmetry cannot fill all of them.

Open a window to see the named gate. A gravity route may need new coefficient-selection structure; a cosmological claim needs one model with common parameters across different observations. The map records these boundaries rather than offering a simulated sky as their evidence.

An unfinished observatory can still be useful. It can tell us which calculation, observation or independent check would make a proposal more identifying—and which previously exhausted route should not be repeated without a new datum.

Frontier physics target set

The target map keeps physical identification, coefficient selection, common-parameter cosmology and continuum limits as distinct gates. A target or workflow priority is not confirmation of new physics. The observatory offers questions, not simulated observations.
